previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary atherosclerosis, prior myocardial infarction, coronary stent placement, and chronic hepatitis C, presented with chest pain and signs of neck cellulitis. He was evaluated in the emergency department, where the chest pain was deemed non-acute based on stable EKG and clinical assessment, and the neck infection was diagnosed as cellulitis requiring IV antibiotics. Despite medical advice to remain for observation and treatment, the patient elected to leave against medical advice after a brief evaluation. He was prescribed oral antibiotics and advised to follow up promptly with his primary care and cardiology providers. The hospital course was minimal due to the early departure.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ yo M with a PMH s/f CAD s/p DES to LAD and 
polysubstance abuse who presents with chest pain for several 
days.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
Chest pain: On admission Mr. ___ was given aspirin, plavix, 
morphine and was started on a heparin drip. He refused NTG as he 
says it gives him a severe headache. He was also retarted on his 
home metoprolol, statin, and lisinopril. His pain resolved by 
the morning and he did not report SOB or nausea. His CEs were 
negative 3 and his EKG showed NSR, axis leftward, PR interval 
borderline, Q waves V1-V4 with poor R wave progression, ST 
elevations V1-V3 which were all present on his EKG one month 
ago. His echo showed new apical/distal anterior/septal regional 
wall motion abnormalities which were felt to be in a similar 
distribution as his prior LAD DES. Because of these findings and 
his non-compliance with his plavix and aspirin it was thought 
that he may have an occlusion of his stent though his negative 
CEs and stable EKG suggest this was not acutely occluded. It was 
decided that he would be a poor candidate for intervention since 
he would ___ not be compliant with his medications in the 
future. His medications were refilled and he was discharged.

Heroin abuse/withdrawal: On admission the patient stated that he 
had not used heroin or other drugs for several years. The 
following morning he stated that he was withdrawing from heroin 
and reported that he had been using 2G a day for several months. 
He repeatedly asked to leave but was talked into staying. He was 
given ativan and clonidine with some improvement in his 
agitation. Though he expressed a desire to go to rehabilitation 
he refused to wait for a bed to be secured for him saying that 
he would find a bed himself. Despite encouragement to stay he 
decided that he would leave and attempt to secure placement by 
himself.

Medication noncompliance: Currently homeless. He reports that he 
had not been taking his medications because they had been stolen 
from him. Would likely benefit from social services. Current 
heroin use likely contributing. 

INACTIVE ISSUES:
HTN: BPs mildly elevated on admission and he was restarted on 
his home dose of lisinopril and metoprolol. BPs were well 
controlled in the hospital. His medications were refilled and 
given to him on discharge.

Discharge Instructions:
Mr. ___,

You were transferred to ___ for further evaluation of your 
chest pain.  Your EKG (electrocardiogram) did not show any 
changes, and lab tests showed you did not have a heart attack.  
However, an ultrasound of your heart showed that the heart 
muscle is not working as well as it should be, likely due to 
your prior heart attacks.  We are also concerned that one or 
more of your stents may be blocked, since you have been off of 
your medications including aspirin and Plavix.

For now, we recommend continuing to treat you with medications.  
Please restart taking aspirin, clopidogrel (plavix), 
pravastatin, lisinopril, and metoprolol succinate for your heart 
disease.  Please follow-up with your primary care doctor and 
your cardiologist.  If you do not continue taking the 
medications, you will be at an even higher risk of having 
another heart attack.

While you were here, you also experienced withdrawal symptoms 
from heroin.  We strongly urged you to stay until we were able 
to find a detoxification ___ you to go to, but you 
preferred to be discharged home and arrange admission to a detox 
center on your own.  It is very important that you seek 
additional treatment for your addiction, and our Social Work 
department provided you with information about centers that you 
may be able to go to.  

Please restart the following medications:
Aspirin 325mg daily
Plavix (clopidogrel) 75mg daily
Lisinopril 5mg daily
Pravastatin 40mg daily
Metoprolol succinate 25mg daily

You should also continue taking citalopram and an albuterol 
inhaler.

Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.
